Traditional Mince Pies

Served at: St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Makes 12 piesPrep 30 minCook 20 min

Mince pies are a quintessential British Christmas treat, traditionally enjoyed throughout the festive season and often continuing into St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day). These sweet, spiced fruit pies, encased in buttery shortcrust pastry, are a delightful way to continue the holiday cheer, often served with a cup of tea or a festive drink as families gather for continued celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 2 ¼ cups (270g) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • ¾ cup (170g) unsalted butter, very cold and cut into small cubes
  • ¼ cup (60ml) ice water, plus more if needed
  • 1 ½ cups (350g) good quality mincemeat
  • 1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon milk (for egg wash)
  • 2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar (icing sugar), for dusting

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt.
  2. Add the cold, cubed butter to the flour mixture. Using your fingertips or a pastry blender, cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining.
  3. Gradually add the ice water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Be careful not to overmix. Form the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
  4. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
  5. On a lightly floured surface, roll out about two-thirds of the chilled pastry to a thickness of about ⅛ inch (3mm).
  6. Using a 3-inch (7.5cm) round cookie cutter, cut out 12 circles for the pie bases. Carefully press each circle into the prepared muffin tin cups.
  7. Spoon about 1 to 1 ½ tablespoons of mincemeat into each pastry-lined cup.
  8. Roll out the remaining pastry. Using a smaller cookie cutter (about 2 inches / 5cm, or a festive shape like a star), cut out 12 tops for the pies.
  9. Place a pastry top over the mincemeat filling in each cup. You can gently press the edges to seal if using full circles, or simply place the star on top.
  10. Brush the tops of the pies with the egg wash.
  11. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.
  12. Let the mince pies cool in the muffin tin for 5 minutes before carefully transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
  13. Once cooled, dust generously with confectioners' sugar before serving.

Tips

  • For an extra festive touch, add a pinch of orange zest or a teaspoon of brandy to your store-bought mincemeat before filling the pies.
  • Mince pies are delicious served warm with a dollop of brandy butter, clotted cream, or vanilla ice cream.
  • Unbaked mince pies can be frozen for up to 3 months. Place them on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a freezer bag. Bake from frozen, adding about 5-10 minutes to the baking time.
